passages.title: A Weekend Workshop: Essential Tools for Home Repairs and DIY Projects
passages.titleVi: Xưởng làm việc cuối tuần: Những dụng cụ thiết yếu cho sửa chữa nhà cửa và các dự án tự làm
passages.text: Every Saturday morning, Marcus opens his garage workshop to repair household furniture and build practical woodwork. On his sturdy workbench, he keeps a durable steel hammer ready to drive nails smoothly into tough oak boards. Along the workshop wall, he installed heavy-duty brass hooks to hang hand tools, measuring tapes, and coiled extension cords neatly. To inspect the upper ceiling joints and clear roof gutters, he climbs a portable aluminum ladder with non-slip rubber feet. When lifting heavy wooden frames, Marcus uses a steel pry bar as a mechanical lever to multiply his physical lifting force. His grandfather gave him an antique bench vise with a rotating iron crank that secures rough wooden planks firmly in position. While splitting dense firewood logs for the outdoor fireplace, he drives a tapered steel wedge directly into the grain. Marcus also inspects the copper plumbing pipes under the sink to prevent any persistent water drip from damaging cabinet wood. He uses an adjustable wrench to tighten loose pipe fittings, securing the brass connectors against unexpected plumbing leaks. To transport bulky boxes of ceramic tiles across the garage floor, he loads them onto a rolling four-wheel dolly. Before applying a fresh coat of protective varnish, he wipes the wood surface with a cloth dampened in mineral paint thinner. His patient craftsmanship allows him to mend old broken chairs and restore faded family heirlooms with genuine pride and care. Marcus organizes spare replacement parts in labeled plastic bins so that every bolt, washer, and nut is instantly accessible. Learning to handle versatile hand tools empowers homeowners to maintain their living spaces safely, efficiently, and independently over time.

pronunciationNotesVi: thinner (/ˈθɪn.ɚ/): Âm đầu là âm th thổi vô thanh /θ/ (đặt đầu lưỡi giữa hai hàm răng và đẩy luồng hơi ra), không phát âm thành âm /t/ hay /s/. Trọng âm rơi vào âm tiết đầu.
tighten (/ˈtaɪ.tən/): Chứa nguyên âm đôi /aɪ/ và âm mũi /n/. Trong tiếng Anh-Mỹ tự nhiên, âm /t/ thứ hai thường được phát âm thành âm nghẹn thanh hầu (glottal stop [ʔ]) trước âm tiết mũi /ən/.

lever (/ˈlev.ɚ/ hoặc /ˈliː.vɚ/): Trong tiếng Anh-Mỹ, từ này thường phát âm với nguyên âm ngắn /e/ (/ˈlev.ɚ/), khác với tiếng Anh-Anh vốn chuộng nguyên âm dài /iː/ (/ˈliː.və/). Trọng âm nhấn ở âm tiết đầu.
crank (/kræŋk/): Tổ hợp phụ âm đầu /kr/ phát âm liền mạch, nguyên âm /æ/ đi trước phụ âm mũi ngạc mềm /ŋ/ tạo độ mở vang tự nhiên, kết thúc dứt khoát bằng âm bật vô thanh /k/.
